_README: Calibration cases for the audio-listening tooling: pairs where a HUMAN's
verdict is on record, so the metrics can be checked against something
Audio is NOT committed. Each case records how to REGENERATE its artifacts
(a git commit to build at, plus the builder invocation), following this
project's existing pattern of regenerating fixtures rather than storing
always, and checks the measured claims only when the artifacts are present.
To add a case: append to `cases`. No new test code is needed.

cases.human_verdict: something with the perc or drums
cases.verdict_source: docs/guides/AUDIO_TIGHTNESS_GUIDE.md (the case that motivated sidm2/audio_tightness.py); docs/players/BLACKBIRD.md B13 entry

bad.commit_subject: Blackbird Stage B12+B13: instrument-select restart timing + gate-off/note translator fix
bad.note: The build the human listened to. Its 'drums sound off' cause was later root-caused and fixed by ef3263b (B25) and 12c7da5 (E3e).

repeatability_floor_pct.description: Original vs a re-render of ITSELF at perturbed power-on delays. The metric's own noise band on this material -- nothing at or above it is evidence.

findings.summary: The metric ranks the known-bad build below the known-good one (56.9 < 64.7), so it has ORDINAL sensitivity. It has no usable ABSOLUTE calibration: a 99.8%-register-exact build with 162/162 note-ons still scores 64.7%, more than 20 points below the 85-91% original-vs-itself floor. Any threshold that flags the known-bad build also flags the known-good one. Further, the 7.8-point gap between builds is comparable to the floor's own 5.9-point spread, so a single A/B run cannot separate them confidently.
